summary: Village streets, parkway trees and storm debris go through Public Works. Trees fully on private property are the owner's job. Companies doing parkway tree work must register as contractors with the Building Department.

contacts.name: Public Works
contacts.hours: Mon-Fri 7am-3pm. After hours, call the police non-emergency line and they relay to Public Works.
contacts.notes: Streets, branch and brush pickup, storm debris. Parkway tree removal requests go here too. Village crews pick up limbs; large trunks need a private company.

contacts.name: Building Department
contacts.notes: Contractor registration: General $125, most trades $75, with a bond and insurance on file. The Lansing Journal (Sept 2026) says parkway tree work requires a registered contractor. No separate tree-removal permit was found.

contacts.name: Mayor (Village President)
contacts.notes: Reach him through the Village Hall main line.

contacts.name: Police non-emergency
contacts.notes: Call this number to report a tree blocking a street or sidewalk. Call 911 for emergencies.

contacts.name: Thornton Township Highway Dept
contacts.notes: Unincorporated township roads only. Village streets belong to Lansing Public Works.

contacts.name: Refuse hauler (Homewood Disposal)
contacts.notes: Branches go at the front curb on garbage day. No pickup in alleys.

notFound: Not found: a village emergency management office, a forestry or arborist contact, a Public Works email, and solicitor-permit rules for door-to-door sales.
